body:
- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

See [this](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/1811) discussion.

`recent_files` has been optimized to stop adding files to the collection to be displayed when the required number of files have already been added.
This prevents unnecessary calls to `vim.fn.filereadable(f)`.

comment_data.body:
This can be simplified

```suggestion
      -- Use only actual readable files possibly respecting current directory
      local is_readable = vim.fn.filereadable(f) == 1
      local is_in_dir = not current_dir or f:find(cwd_pattern) ~= nil
      if is_readable and is_in_dir then
        n_added = n_added + 1
        table.insert(files, f)
      end

      if n_added >= n then break end
```
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -524,29 +524,35 @@ MiniStarter.sections.recent_files = function(n, current_dir, show_path)
 
   return function()
     local section = string.format('Recent files%s', current_dir and ' (current directory)' or '')
-
-    -- Use only actual readable files
-    local files = vim.tbl_filter(function(f) return vim.fn.filereadable(f) == 1 end, vim.v.oldfiles or {})
-
-    if #files == 0 then
-      return { { name = 'There are no recent files (`v:oldfiles` is empty)', action = '', section = section } }
-    end
-
-    -- Possibly filter files from current directory
-    if current_dir then
-      local sep = vim.loop.os_uname().sysname == 'Windows_NT' and [[%\]] or '%/'
-      local cwd_pattern = '^' .. vim.pesc(vim.fn.getcwd()) .. sep
-      -- Use only files from current directory and its subdirectories
-      files = vim.tbl_filter(function(f) return f:find(cwd_pattern) ~= nil end, files)
+    local sep = vim.loop.os_uname().sysname == 'Windows_NT' and [[%\]] or '%/'
+    local cwd_pattern = '^' .. vim.pesc(vim.fn.getcwd()) .. sep
+
+    local n_added = 0
+    local files = {}
+    for _, f in ipairs(vim.v.oldfiles) do
+      if n_added == n then break end
+
+      -- Use only actual readable files
+      local add = vim.fn.filereadable(f) == 1
+      if current_dir then
+        -- Filter files from current directory and its subdirectories
+        add = add and f:find(cwd_pattern) ~= nil
+      end
+      if add then
+        n_added = n_added + 1
+        table.insert(files, f)
+      end

comment_regular_data.body:
Thanks again for the PR!

It looks good in general, I'll just add some finishing touches before merging into `main`.
This is now [part of the `main` branch](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/commit/4357160712c8e2c80318d46a827bf972fca24d61). Thanks again for the PR!

Thank you! I noticed that you rewrote the test removing the screenshot. An improvement indeed! Putting the `#files > n` inside the `if` is also much better.

New challenge: Create a PR where every line is exactly right...)))

I only somewhat later realized that this (and probably some others) test can be done without screenshot and have almost similar amount of coverage.

> New challenge: Create a PR where every line is exactly right...)))

You've already achieved that in #1671 :)

But yeah, sorry, I do understand that this somewhat extreme obsession over code might drive away contributions. My current approach is to mostly target the PR to the point where all the rest of changes are nitpicks. Beyond that it is easier for both parties if I quickly add them myself.

> But yeah, sorry...

No apologies needed! It's a privilege to learn from you. I have the same obsession over code.
